findings.desc: Migration backfill made historical closed reworks emit terminalDisposition, breaking the exact legacy generator list wire during rollout.
An unhandled decision fetch or successor-start failure could reject the coordinator tick and starve unrelated candidates.
The legacy local cancel path still allowed a review-aware READY candidate to bypass the server-owned accept-or-rework state machine.
A device authorization created after an accept decision was pre-approved, weakening the existing exact-device Telegram approval boundary.
The accept receipt projected an unbounded authorization history even though feed and generator clients cap response collections at 100 items.
Requiring an append-only decision before release approval removes the old Feed approval path during a backend-before-Feed rolling window.
The generator client accepted source identifiers outside the backend playable-id namespace, creating a late successor handoff rejection.
Opening the rework form had no escape path, making the accept outcome unreachable without reloading the Mini App.

dispositions.reason: This is an intentional fail-closed compatibility break: restoring legacy approval would reopen an unfenced path around the append-only decision. The bounded rollout order is Feed, then Generator, then Backend; candidate actions remain paused until all three are healthy.
